component.name: rest
component.title: REST
component.description: Expose REST services or call external REST services.
component.label: core,rest

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

consumerComponentName.label: consumer
consumerComponentName.description: The name of the Camel component that runs the REST services, such as platform-http, servlet or jetty. The consumerComponentName option of an endpoint replaces it. If neither is set, the component of the rest configuration is used.

apiDoc.label: producer
apiDoc.description: The location of the OpenAPI document (JSON or YAML) of the REST service to call: a file, an http or https URL, or a classpath resource. The apiDoc option of an endpoint replaces it. If neither is set, the producerApiDoc of the rest configuration is used.

host.label: producer
host.description: The scheme, host and port of the REST service to call, with an optional base path, such as http://myserver:8080/foo. The host option of an endpoint replaces it. If neither is set, the host and port of the rest configuration are used.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

producerComponentName.label: producer
producerComponentName.description: The name of the Camel component that sends the HTTP requests, such as http or vertx-http. The producerComponentName option of an endpoint replaces it. If neither is set, the producerComponent of the rest configuration is used.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

headerFilterStrategy.label: filter
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.spi.HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

CamelRestHttpQuery.label: producer
CamelRestHttpQuery.description: The query string of the request. The producer sets it from the queryParameters option, with the {name} values filled in. The HTTP producer uses it in place of the query of its endpoint.

CamelRestHttpUri.label: producer
CamelRestHttpUri.description: The URI of the request, with the path parameters filled in. The producer sets it when it fills a path parameter from a header or a variable, and then removes the CamelHttpPath header. The HTTP producer uses it in place of the URI of its endpoint.

CamelHttpMethod.label: producer
CamelHttpMethod.description: The HTTP method of the request, in upper case. The producer sets it from the method of the endpoint, and replaces any value that the message has.

Content-Type.label: producer
Content-Type.description: The media type of the request body. The producer sets it to the produces option when the message has no Content-Type header. With binding, the producer reads it to choose between JSON and XML.

Accept.label: producer
Accept.description: The media types that the response may have. The producer sets it to the consumes option when the message has no Accept header.

CamelHttpResponseCode.label: producer
CamelHttpResponseCode.description: The HTTP status code of the response, which the HTTP producer sets. With binding, the producer does not read a response with a code of 300 or more into outType, unless skipBindingOnErrorCode of the rest configuration is false.

consumerOut.description: The request body as the HTTP consumer gives it (platform-http by default). With bindingMode json, the object of inType, or a Map or a List without inType

consumerReply.description: The response body as the HTTP consumer writes it. With bindingMode json, any object, which the binding writes as JSON

producerIn.description: The request body the HTTP producer sends (the http component by default). With bindingMode json, any object, which the binding writes as JSON

producerOut.description: The response body as the HTTP producer gives it; with bindingMode json and outType, an object of outType

method.label: common
method.description: The HTTP method of the REST service. The consumer answers requests with this method, and the producer sends the request with it.

path.label: common
path.description: The base path of the REST service, such as users. Without uriTemplate, it is the whole path, and it can hold {name} path parameters as in uriTemplate. A consumer can end it with * to match all the paths that start with it.

uriTemplate.label: common
uriTemplate.description: The path below the base path, such as {id}, which can hold {name} path parameters. The consumer sets each path parameter of a request as a header. The producer fills each {name} with the header of that name, or else the exchange variable of that name.

consumes.label: common
consumes.description: The media types, separated by comma, that this endpoint takes in, such as application/json. For the consumer, the media types of the request body that the REST service accepts. The producer sets it as the Accept header of the request when the message has no Accept header.

inType.label: common
inType.description: The class name of the request body, with [] appended for an array. The consumer stores it in the rest registry. With xml binding, the producer uses it as the JAXB context of the request body.

outType.label: common
outType.description: The class name of the response body, with [] appended for an array. With a binding mode other than off, the producer reads a JSON or XML response into this class, and without it the producer does not read the response. The consumer stores it in the rest registry.

produces.label: common
produces.description: The media types, separated by comma, that this endpoint sends, such as application/json. For the consumer, the media types of the response body that the REST service returns. The producer sets it as the Content-Type header of the request when the message has no Content-Type header.

routeId.label: common
routeId.description: The id of the route of this REST service, which the consumer stores in the rest registry to count the requests of the service. The Rest DSL sets it to the id of the route that it creates. This option does not set the id of the route.

consumerComponentName.label: consumer
consumerComponentName.description: The name of the Camel component that runs the REST service, such as platform-http, servlet or jetty. If not set, the component of the rest configuration is used. If that is not set either, the consumer takes the first component of the CamelContext that is a RestConsumerFactory, then platform-http, then a single RestConsumerFactory in the registry, then servlet, jetty, undertow, netty-http or coap, whichever is on the classpath.

description.label: consumer
description.description: A description of this REST service, which the consumer stores in the rest registry. The Rest DSL sets it from the description of the route, the verb or the rest.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

apiDoc.label: producer
apiDoc.description: The location of the OpenAPI document (JSON or YAML) of the REST service to call: a file, an http or https URL, or a classpath resource. When set, the producer needs camel-openapi-java, and fails to start if the document has no operation for the method and path. If not set, the apiDoc option of the component, or else the producerApiDoc of the rest configuration, is used.

bindingMode.label: producer
bindingMode.description: The binding mode of the producer, which replaces the bindingMode of the rest configuration (off by default). With json, xml or json_xml, the producer writes a POJO body as JSON or XML, and reads the response into outType. With auto, it chooses from the Content-Type header, and sends or keeps a body that it cannot bind as it is.

host.label: producer
host.description: The scheme, host and port of the REST service to call, with an optional base path, such as http://myserver:8080/foo. The scheme is http when it is not given. If not set, the host option of the component, or else the host and port of the rest configuration, is used. The producer fails to start without a host.

producerComponentName.label: producer
producerComponentName.description: The name of the Camel component that sends the HTTP request, such as http or vertx-http. If not set, the producerComponent of the rest configuration is used. If that is not set either, the producer takes the first component of the CamelContext that is a RestProducerFactory, then the component of consumerComponentName, then a single RestProducerFactory in the registry, then http, vertx-http, undertow or netty-http, whichever is on the classpath.

queryParameters.label: producer
queryParameters.description: The query string of the request, such as foo=123&bar=456. A value {name} is filled with the header or the exchange variable of that name, and a parameter with the value {name?} is left out when neither is set. The endpoint also adds the parameters of its URI that it does not know, except the options of the component that sends the HTTP request.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.
